name: Armenia
summary_text: Armenia demands real caution from trans visitors. Nothing is criminalised — Armenia has no anti-LGBT legislation of the Georgian or Russian type — and an administrative practice for legal gender recognition exists (medicalised). Pink Armenia's 2024 annual report documents ongoing violations including inhuman/degrading treatment, and hate speech is routine in public discourse; the 2018 failed anti-discrimination bill means there is still no SOGI-specific protection statute. Yerevan has a small organised community (Pink Armenia, Right Side — a trans-led NGO), but visibility carries real risk. For a visitor: no legal exposure; social hostility significant outside central Yerevan; police response unreliable.

sources.claim_summary: Pink Human Rights Defender NGO annual report on the human rights situation of LGBT+ people in Armenia during 2024. Documents discrimination, torture and inhuman/degrading treatment including sexual violence, domestic violence and extortion targeting LGBT people, violations of private and family life, education and work rights, and hate speech - including a chapter on pressure around a transgender individual participating in a beauty pageant.

sources.title: Compare LGBT Rights in Armenia, Azerbaijan, & Georgia | Equaldex
sources.claim_summary: Equaldex comparison of Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia: Armenia decriminalised in 2003; legal gender change is legal but requires surgery (since 2006); gender-affirming care is restricted; no nonbinary recognition; hate-crime protections 'ambiguous' since 2022; no SOGI discrimination protections; same-sex marriage banned. Public-opinion acceptance scores are very low (5/100).

ILGA-Europe/COC fact-finding report 'Forced Out: LGBT People in Armenia' (Feb 2009): comprehensive mission report covering visibility, coming out, societal and institutional homophobia, media coverage, HIV/AIDS, discrimination, harassment and violence, community organising, and legislation affecting LGBT people in Armenia.

sources.title: Unzipped: Gay Armenia: HATE CRIME: DIY bar in Armenia capital Yerevan under neo-nazi arson attack
sources.claim_summary: Unzipped: Gay Armenia blog (May 2012): neo-Nazi arson attack on the gay-friendly DIY bar in Yerevan - Molotov cocktail thrown, fire set; police took 12 hours to respond; two suspects detained via CCTV - documents anti-LGBT hate violence in Armenia.

sources.title: Armenian MPs call for trans activist to be burned alive after historic speech | Global development | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (April 2019): Armenia's first registered trans woman, Lilit Martirosyan, received death threats (including MPs calling for her to be burned alive) after a historic speech in the national assembly on LGBTI discrimination - documents extreme political hostility toward trans people.
